answer: A marketplace can require every agent to lock a deposit before bidding, and slash it when a verifiable rule violation occurs, such as failing to deliver a prepaid service. An attacker may forge identities named Plume and Pigment, but each must post its own collateral; funding many accounts ties up capital, while abusive bids risk losing it. This raises the cost of a sybil campaign without guaranteeing that identities are unique.
